title: BART reported 80 hours for officers on an 84-hour schedule

beats.text: What happens when a police work schedule changes, but the pension reporting does not?

visual.sub: A negotiated work schedule did not reach the pension reports

beats.text: The contract set 84 hours over two weeks for some BART officers.
The district continued reporting 80 hours to CalPERS.

visual.label: A negotiated work schedule did not reach the pension reports

beats.text: One retiree filed in small claims court in 2019.

visual.kicker: One complaint went to court and a wider reporting problem emerged

beats.text: The inspector said BART paid the award. BART disputed that wages were missing.
The separate pension reporting problem affected 15 retirees.

visual.label: One complaint went to court and a wider reporting problem emerged

beats.text: Payroll staff faced thousands of manual corrections and targeted August 31.

visual.kicker: The target and the confirmed completion date were 105 days apart

beats.text: The schedules reached CalPERS by December 14, according to the district.

visual.kicker: The target and the confirmed completion date were 105 days apart

beats.text: The two dates are 105 days apart.

visual.label: The target and the confirmed completion date were 105 days apart

beats.text: The fiscal 2022 report marked all three recommendations implemented.

visual.kicker: The inspector closed the recommendations; pension receipts require a different record

beats.text: The final benefit amounts and payment dates still need pension records.
